medium.source: standard reference value at 20 C (fresh water, seawater) or ISA sea level (air); the same values sim-engine/validate/locomotion/media.json carries, with the same caveat that mucus, biofilm and sediment pore water are far more viscous

result.model: Stokes drag, F = 6*pi*mu*a*v. Exact for a sphere in the creeping limit.
result.model_caveat: Drag on an isolated sphere in an unbounded fluid. A particle resting on a surface also has friction and adhesion, which are often LARGER than the drag and are not modelled here; particles in a pile shield one another, which this does not model either; and a non-spherical particle has a different coefficient. Treat the force here as a lower bound on what the task needs.
what_this_cannot_say: whether the design can GET to the particle, aim at it, or hold on to it: there is no control model
whether a pile forms: moving particles and accumulating them are different problems, and the second is about where they are released
how long it would take, or whether the organism can pay for it

result.scope: What the design accomplishes, as distinct from its shape or its gait. Three checks, each resting on something that cannot be argued with -- a constant-hazard expectation, Stokes drag, and conservation of mass -- evaluated over quantities the caller declares with sources. It models no mechanism: it does not say HOW the organism would live longer, exert a force or fix carbon, only whether the numbers a designer states are consistent with each other and with physics. A design this layer does not contradict has not been shown to work.
